raw_comment:
I notice that locations with higher elevations have lower humidity levels. This is likely due to their distance from the ocean.  However, there are higher drought levels than anticipated in a few places along the East Coast.

I wonder why areas like New York and Delaware are recorded to have less humidity when they are almost directly on the water.

I live in a mountainous region, and we are regularly in droughts so it's surprising to see that we aren't at the dryest level when we regularly have a large lack of humidity.

Title: Hawaii: the not so Tropical Punch.
